cases.name: Leopold Aschenbrenner
cases.rise: An AI-focused fund manager whose fast-growing portfolio made him a prominent name in the AI investment boom.
cases.fall: A sell-off in chip stocks hit concentrated, leveraged positions. Margin calls forced the fund to seek fresh capital or sell holdings, bringing it close to collapse.
cases.context: A severe fund drawdown. The reporting does not establish a total fund wipeout or the loss of his entire personal fortune.
cases.lesson: Borrowing can force an investor to sell before a long-term thesis has time to play out.

cases.name: David Chau
cases.metricLabel: Estimated group trading losses over Christmas week
cases.rise: Built a following of roughly 1,000 traders around an S&P 500 options strategy promoted as a reliable source of income.
cases.fall: The group increased its bets after losses using a Martingale approach. The strategy broke down on Christmas Eve, wiping out most or all of participants’ trading capital.
cases.context: The estimate covers the group, not Chau alone. Some followers lost their life savings; his full personal net worth is not established.
cases.lesson: A long winning streak can conceal the risk of one oversized losing trade.

sources.title: The Captain Condor wipeout, reported by MarketWatch and republished by Tiger Brokers

cases.name: James Wynn
cases.metricLabel: Trading profits erased before the account liquidation
cases.rise: A speculative trader who attracted an audience with a spectacular winning streak and enormous Bitcoin positions.
cases.fall: Highly leveraged trades unraveled even with relatively small Bitcoin price moves. CoinDesk reported a reversal from about $100 million in profit to a $17.5 million net trading loss.
cases.context: This was a trading-account liquidation. The net loss figure is not evidence of a personal debt balance or the loss of every asset he owned.
cases.lesson: With enough leverage, a small market move can erase an entire trading account.

sources.title: How James Wynn’s $100M implosion became a leverage lesson

cases.name: Sam Bankman-Fried
cases.metricLabel: Bloomberg’s estimated personal wealth at the collapse
cases.rise: A celebrated crypto entrepreneur and trading-firm founder whose holdings put him among the industry’s wealthiest figures.
cases.fall: FTX and Alameda collapsed, and Bloomberg marked his estimated fortune down to effectively zero within days. A subsequent criminal case established the misuse of customer money.
cases.context: The wealth estimate reflects the value of his holdings, not $16 billion of cash lost in one trade. This case involved fraud as well as risky investments.
cases.lesson: An impressive valuation cannot substitute for trustworthy custody and financial controls.

cases.name: Su Zhu & Kyle Davies
cases.metricLabel: Reported amount owed to creditors in December 2023
cases.rise: Led one of crypto’s most prominent investment firms. Zhu’s market commentary had earned him a guru-like following.
cases.fall: Losses in Terra/Luna and other investments, alongside heavy borrowing, ended in liquidation. Liquidators later pursued assets to repay billions owed to creditors.
cases.context: The figure is creditor debt, not a measured trading loss. The fund failed; neither founder’s entire personal fortune is established as wiped out.
cases.lesson: Correlated bets and borrowed money can turn a market downturn into insolvency.

cases.name: Bill Hwang
cases.metricLabel: Archegos assets at its peak, before the collapse
cases.rise: A former Tiger Management investor whose family office built approximately $160 billion of stock exposure on $36 billion of assets.
cases.fall: Concentrated bets fell, banks demanded additional collateral, and Archegos could not meet those demands. Banks sold the positions. Hwang was convicted of fraud and market manipulation in 2024.
cases.context: Hwang lost the bulk of his personal fortune. The $36 billion figure is peak firm assets, not a precise measure of his personal loss.
cases.lesson: Concentration and leverage can overwhelm even decades of investing experience.
